extracted.intended_audience: Scholars and project teams (PIs, Co-PIs, collaborators, administering organizations) preparing Vision Grant proposals to the Spencer Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing a Spencer Foundation Vision Grant proposal: a $75,000, 6–12 month planning grant to collaboratively design large-scale, interdisciplinary education research aimed at transforming systems for equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose: transform educational systems for equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vision Grants program funds the collaborative planning of innovative, methodologically diverse, interdisciplinary research on education that contributes to transforming education systems for equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be geared toward real-world impact on equity, envision how systems-change will happen using research evidence, and focus on transforming educational systems toward greater equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning-grant scope (not a fully fleshed research plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Grants are research planning grants to bring together a team for 6 to 12 months to collaboratively develop ambitious, large-scale research projects; the proposal should not be a fully fleshed out research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of a complete study protocol, proposals should 'think forward' about the research needed to transform systems — identifying topic, initial design ideas, impact planning, collaboration processes, and a team that will lead to a fully fleshed plan by grant end. The Foundation is not looking for planning grants where the research design is already fleshed out and the team seeks funding for pre-study activities such as instrument design or obtaining IRB approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify targeted system(s) and specific levers for change
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should identify the system(s) targeted for transformation and the specific levers the team thinks need to be engaged in order to work toward systems transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate which parts of the system will be addressed and how engagement of particular levers is expected to produce system-level change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research topic and initial scope/methodological approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must explicitly identify a research topic and initial thoughts about the scope and methodological approach of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide initial conceptualization of study designs and methods (recognizing plans are preliminary for the planning grant stage), and how methodological diversity or interdisciplinarity will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for impact: specify levers for systems change
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include the plan for impact, identifying the levers for systems change that will likely be engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how evidence from eventual research could be used to actually transform systems and what mechanisms or actors will be engaged to drive change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration process: how the team will work together
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must describe the collaboration process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail processes for decision-making, equitable collaboration, roles and responsibilities, and how partners (e.g., practitioners, policymakers, community members) will be meaningfully involved from the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and readiness to produce a full plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should present a team that will lead to a fully fleshed out research plan by the end of the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams are encouraged to be interdisciplinary and/or multi-method and to include collaborators across sectors (researchers, practitioners, policymakers, young people, educators, non-profits, governments, communities). While additional collaborators may be added during planning, proposals are expected to name specific collaborators who have already agreed to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary and multi-method expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Grant teams are expected to be interdisciplinary and/or multi-method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program values methodological and disciplinary diversity as core elements of planning research that can transform systems for equity; propose methods appropriate to ambitious, large-scale aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful and equitable collaboration with partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must rely on meaningful and equitable collaboration with practitioners, policymakers, communities, and other partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should reflect on the people who need to be involved from the beginning of the research design process and show how those partners will be engaged equitably and meaningfully throughout planning and eventual research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name specific collaborators at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of submission, proposals are expected to name specific collaborators across sectors who have already agreed to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although teams may add collaborators during planning, the submission should identify concrete partners to demonstrate genuine collaborative capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include resources for partnership/community development in budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal budgets should include time and resources for the development of partnerships and relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget line items should reflect support for collaboration-building activities; see Budget and Budget Justification section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limit and indirect cost policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed budgets for this program are limited to $75,000 total and may not include indirect cost charges per Spencer’s policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Applicant Information and Policies for full budget rules. Vision Grants are $75,000 total; budgets must be in U.S. Dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vision Grant may not be longer than 12 months in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical planning projects should be scoped to complete within the 6–12 month grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI/Co-PI eligibility and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators (PIs) and Co-PIs must have appropriate experience or an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or a terminal degree in a professional field; graduate students may not be named PI or Co-PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate PI/Co-PI capacity to lead planning of ambitious, large-scale, interdisciplinary research; experience and credentials matter for reviewer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organization affiliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution willing to serve as the administering organization if the grant is awarded; Spencer does not award grants directly to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include colleges, universities, school districts, research facilities, or other non-profit organizations with appropriate non-profit status (e.g., 501(c)(3) in the U.S. or equivalent outside the U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and currency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are accepted from the U.S. and internationally; all proposals must be submitted in English and budgets must be proposed in U.S. Dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project teams do not have to include U.S.-based scholars or partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on PI/Co-PI participation across proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may not be part of more than one Vision Grant proposal (funded and/or in review). Additionally, a PI or Co-PI cannot be part of a Transformative Research Grant and apply for another Vision Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction marks a change from earlier cycles; follow current policy when assembling teams and planning submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness requirement from other Spencer proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: If PIs/Co-PIs have another active Spencer grant or proposal in review, the projects proposed in a Vision Grant proposal and in another Spencer grant program proposal must be distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may have concurrent Spencer-funded work, but proposed projects must not duplicate or be the same project across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded activities (what Vision Grants do not fund)
rubrics_metrics.description: Across Spencer programs, and Vision Grants are no exception, the Foundation does not fund activities like program evaluation, capital campaigns, the creation or maintenance of research centers, or scholarships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, Spencer is not looking for planning grants where the research design is already fleshed out and the team seeks funding for pre-study activities such as design of study instrumentation and securing IRB approval and permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review panel composition and review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Grant proposals will be reviewed by a panel of senior scholars and other senior partners (e.g., practitioners, policymakers, leaders of community-based organizations) who have extensive experience designing and collaborating on research projects aimed to transform systems toward equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess the proposal’s potential for transformative impact on equity, the plausibility of the plan for impact, the strength and equity of collaborations, methodological and disciplinary breadth, and the team’s capacity to develop a full research plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Grant proposals may be resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow resubmission guidance and deadlines in the Applicant Information and Policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Transformative Research Grant (TRG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Being awarded a Vision Grant is a prerequisite for applying to the Transformative Research Grant program (TRG, $3.5M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vision Grant awardees will have the option to apply for TRG; Vision Grantees are eligible to apply for a TRG for up to three years after their Vision Grant is completed. However, receiving a Vision Grant does not obligate grantees to pursue TRG funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special encouragement: AI and Education
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the Initiative on AI and Education, additional funds within the Vision Grant program have been designated for work focused on AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that address AI and education may receive special encouragement; consult program materials for examples and emphasis areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected scale and ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Grants are intended to incubate and plan ambitious, large-scale research projects focused on transforming educational systems for equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate ambition and plausibility for systems-level change and how planning during the grant period will prepare the team for larger-scale implementation or subsequent TRG proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/procedural notes (timelines, number of awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: We expect to award 10 Vision Grants during each cycle of the program, plus several grants focused on AI and Education; there will be two Vision Grant cycles per year; project timelines should not begin until 7–8 months after the proposal deadline to allow for review time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these timelines for planning start dates and downstream proposals; note this is guidance on scheduling rather than an application evaluation criterion.
